body.statement:
Suppose \(h_n\le 1/32\), with \(a_\star=7/10\) and \(b=3/4\).  Then \(J_n\ge2\), the cutoff locations in \(\mathcal W_n\) lie in \([1/4,3/4]\), and the supports of distinct compliance profiles are disjoint up to Lebesgue-null endpoints.  The common potential-outcome table satisfies
\[
 q_{00}(x)=q_{11}(x)=\frac18,
 \qquad
 \frac1{40}\le q_{01}(x),q_{10}(x)\le\frac{29}{40},
 \qquad
 \sum_{u_0,u_1\in\{0,1\}}q_{u_0,u_1}(x)=1.
\]
All twelve latent masses defining every \(P_{j,\ell}\in\mathcal W_n\) are nonnegative and sum to one; the always-taker and never-taker masses are strictly positive everywhere, and the complier masses are strictly positive wherever \(w_{j,\ell}>0\).  No H\"older restriction on these latent cells is used.  The observable one-sided extensions are
\[
 \mu_{D,P_{j,\ell}}^{-}(x)=\frac{1-w_{j,\ell}(x)}2,
 \qquad
 \mu_{D,P_{j,\ell}}^{+}(x)=\frac{1+w_{j,\ell}(x)}2,
\]
\[
 \mu_{Y,P_{j,\ell}}^{-}(x)=\frac12-\frac{g_\star(x)w_{j,\ell}(x)}2,
 \qquad
 \mu_{Y,P_{j,\ell}}^{+}(x)=\frac12+\frac{g_\star(x)w_{j,\ell}(x)}2.
\]
They belong to the radius-\(M\), order-\(s\) H\"older ball.  The potential reduced forms are continuous at \(c_{j,\ell}\), and
\[
 d_{P_{j,\ell}}=\kappa_n,
 \qquad
 \theta_{P_{j,+}}=a_\star=\frac7{10},
 \qquad
 \theta_{P_{j,-}}=-a_\star=-\frac7{10}.
\]
Writing \(p_{j,\ell}^{D,Y}\) and \(p_{j,\ell}^{D}\) for the conditional observable cell probabilities, one has
\[
 p_{j,\ell}^{D,Y}(x,d,y)
 =p_{j,\ell}^{D}(x,d)m_{d,y}(x)
 \ge\frac{21}{320}>v.
\]
On either observable side,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{P_{j,\ell}}(Y\mid X=x)
 =\frac{1-g_\star(x)^2}{4}
  +g_\star(x)^2\operatorname{Var}_{P_{j,\ell}}(D\mid X=x)
 \ge\frac{51}{400}>v,
\]
and, when the treatment variance is positive,
\[
 \left|\operatorname{corr}_{P_{j,\ell}}(Y,D\mid X=x)\right|
 \le\frac7{\sqrt{51}}<\frac{63}{64}\le1-v.
\]
When the treatment variance is zero, the covariance is zero and the model-class convention applies.  Consequently \(\mathcal W_n\subset\mathcal P_n\).  Moreover, with \(R_\star\) as the outcome-invariant reference,
\[
 \frac{dP_{j,\ell}}{dR_\star}
 =1+(2D-1)\operatorname{sgn}(X-c_{j,\ell})w_{j,\ell}(X)
 \quad R_\star\text{-almost surely},
\]
so every product likelihood ratio is measurable with respect to \(\sigma((X_i,D_i)_{i=1}^n)\).  Finally,
\[
 \int_{-1}^{1}\psi(u)^2\,du=\frac{256}{315},
 \qquad
 E_{R_\star}\!\left[
 \frac{dP_{j,\ell}}{dR_\star}
 \frac{dP_{k,r}}{dR_\star}
 \right]=1
\]
for distinct \((j,\ell)\ne(k,r)\), and, for
\(Q_{\ell,n}=J_n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{J_n}P_{j,\ell}^{\otimes n}\),
\[
 \chi^2(Q_{\ell,n},R_\star^{\otimes n})
 =\frac{\left(1+\frac{256}{315}\kappa_n^2h_n\right)^n-1}{J_n}.
\]
body.proof_tex:
Write \(a=a_\star=7/10\) and \(b=3/4\).  We verify each requirement in the order used by the lower bound.

First, \(h_n\le1/32\) implies \((16h_n)^{-1}\ge2\), and hence
\[
 J_n=\left\lfloor(16h_n)^{-1}\right\rfloor\ge2.
 \tag{1}
\]
For \(1\le j\le J_n\), the location formulas in \(\mathrm{def:outcome\mbox{-}invariant\mbox{-}family}\) give
\[
 c_{j,+}-h_n=\frac14+2(j-1)h_n\ge\frac14,
 \qquad
 c_{j,+}+h_n=\frac14+2jh_n\le\frac38,
 \tag{2}
\]
and similarly
\[
 [c_{j,-}-h_n,c_{j,-}+h_n]\subset[5/8,3/4].
 \tag{3}
\]
The centers within either label are separated by \(2h_n\); hence distinct supports meet, at most, at endpoints.  Supports carrying different labels lie in the disjoint plateau intervals in (2)--(3).  Therefore
\[
 w_{j,\ell}(x)w_{k,r}(x)=0
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x
 \quad\text{whenever }(j,\ell)\ne(k,r).
 \tag{4}
\]

Next, \(B'(t)=-30t^2(1-t)^2\le0\), \(B(0)=1\), and \(B(1)=0\).  Thus the definition of \(g_\star\) gives \(|g_\star(x)|\le a\).  With the corrected value \(b=3/4\), the common table is
\[
 q_{00}=q_{11}=\frac18,
 \qquad
 q_{01}=\frac{3/4+g_\star}{2},
 \qquad
 q_{10}=\frac{3/4-g_\star}{2}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Consequently its entries sum to one and
\[
 \min_{u_0,u_1,x}q_{u_0,u_1}(x)
 =\frac{3/4-7/10}{2}=\frac1{40}>0,
 \qquad
 \max_{u_0,u_1,x}q_{u_0,u_1}(x)
 =\frac{3/4+7/10}{2}=\frac{29}{40}.
 \tag{6}
\]
Because \(0\le w_{j,\ell}\le\kappa_n\le1/8\), the latent masses
\[
 \pi_{C,u_0,u_1,P_{j,\ell}}=w_{j,\ell}q_{u_0,u_1},
 \qquad
 \pi_{A,u_0,u_1,P_{j,\ell}}
 =\pi_{N,u_0,u_1,P_{j,\ell}}
 =\frac{1-w_{j,\ell}}2q_{u_0,u_1}
 \tag{7}
\]
are nonnegative.  The latter two are at least
\[
 \frac{1-1/8}{2}\frac1{40}=\frac7{640}>0,
 \tag{8}
\]
and the complier mass is positive wherever \(w_{j,\ell}>0\).  Summing (7) over the four potential-outcome cells and three response types gives
\[
 \sum_{u_0,u_1}q_{u_0,u_1}
 \left(w_{j,\ell}+\frac{1-w_{j,\ell}}2+
                    \frac{1-w_{j,\ell}}2\right)=1.
 \tag{9}
\]
This proves validity of the latent law using positivity alone; no smoothness of an individual latent cell is asserted or needed.

We next check exactly the observable and potential reduced forms that define \(\mathcal P_n\).  The response-type weights in (7) imply
\[
 E[D(z)\mid X=x]=\frac{1-w_{j,\ell}(x)}2+z,w_{j,\ell}(x).
 \tag{10}
\]
The common table (5), which is the same for every response type, gives
\[
 E[Y(0)\mid X=x]=\frac{1-g_\star(x)}2,
 \qquad
 E[Y(1)\mid X=x]=\frac{1+g_\star(x)}2.
 \tag{11}
\]
Combining (10)--(11) yields
\[
 E[Y(D(z))\mid X=x]
 =\frac12+g_\star(x)\left(z-\frac12\right)w_{j,\ell}(x).
 \tag{12}
\]
Equations (10)--(12), consistency, and \(Z=\mathbf 1\{X\ge c_{j,\ell}\}\) give the four displayed observable extensions in the statement.

It remains to verify their H\"older radii without imposing any latent-cell H\"older condition.  On \((-1,1)\),
\[
 \psi'(u)=-4u(1-u^2),
 \qquad
 \psi''(u)=-4+12u^2.
 \tag{13}
\]
Both \(\psi\) and \(\psi'\) join continuously to zero at \(\{-1,1\}\).  Hence
\[
 \lVert\psi'\rVert_\infty\le2,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Lip}(\psi')\le8.
 \tag{14}
\]
When \(s=1\), using \(h_n=32\kappa_n/M\), scaling (14) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Lip}(w_{j,\ell})
 \le\frac{2\kappa_n}{h_n}=\frac{M}{16}.
 \tag{15}
\]
When \(1<s\le2\), put \(\beta=s-1\).  Since \(h_n^s=32\kappa_n/M\), \(h_n\le1\), and a Lipschitz function on an interval of diameter at most one has \(\beta\)-H\"older seminorm bounded by its Lipschitz constant,
\[
 \lVert w_{j,\ell}'\rVert_\infty
 \le\frac{2\kappa_n}{h_n}
 =\frac{M}{16}h_n^{s-1}\le\frac{M}{16},
 \qquad
 [w_{j,\ell}']_{s-1}
 \le\frac{8\kappa_n}{h_n^s}=\frac{M}{4}.
 \tag{16}
\]
By (2)--(3), \(g_\star=a\) on the support of every \(+\) profile and \(g_\star=-a\) on the support of every \(-\) profile.  Since each \(w_{j,\ell}\) vanishes off its support,
\[
 g_\star w_{j,+}=a w_{j,+},
 \qquad
 g_\star w_{j,-}=-a w_{j,-}
 \quad\text{on }[0,1].
 \tag{17}
\]
Thus (15) gives observable Lipschitz constants at most \(M/32\) for treatment and \(aM/32=7M/320\) for outcome.  Equations (16)--(17) give derivative suprema bounded by the same constants and derivative H\"older seminorms at most \(M/8\) and \(aM/8=7M/80\), respectively.  More explicitly, the treatment extensions have supremum norm at most \(9/16\), while the outcome extensions have supremum norm at most \(1/2+a\kappa_n/2\le87/160\).  Hence even under the convention that the radius bounds the sum of the displayed norm components,
\[
 \frac9{16}+\frac{M}{32}+\frac{M}{8}\le M,
 \qquad
 \frac{87}{160}+\frac{7M}{320}+\frac{7M}{80}\le M,
 \tag{18a}
\]
where both inequalities use \(M\ge2\); for \(s=1\), deleting the seminorm term only strengthens them.  Thus each extension lies in the radius-\(M\), order-\(s\) H\"older ball required by \(\mathrm{ass:observable\mbox{-}holder\mbox{-}extensions}\).  Equations (10) and (12) are continuous at \(c_{j,\ell}\), proving the potential-reduced-form continuity condition.

Since \(w_{j,\ell}(c_{j,\ell})=\kappa_n\), the observable treatment extensions give
\[
 d_{P_{j,\ell}}=\kappa_n.
 \tag{18}
\]
The outcome extensions and (17) give
\[
 y_{P_{j,+}}=a\kappa_n,
 \qquad
 y_{P_{j,-}}=-a\kappa_n.
 \tag{19}
\]
The denominator in (18) is positive by \(\kappa_n>0\), so division in the definition of \(\theta_P\) is legitimate, and (18)--(19) yield the two claimed effect labels.  The cutoff is interior by (2)--(3), \(X\) is uniform by construction, and the sample law is the independent product of the displayed one-unit law.

For nondegeneracy, the common table makes the conditional law of \(Y\) given \((D=d,X=x)\) Bernoulli with success probability
\[
 E[Y\mid D=d,X=x]=\frac12+g_\star(x)\left(d-\frac12\right).
 \tag{20}
\]
Thus every conditional outcome margin is at least \((1-a)/2=3/20\).  On either side of the cutoff, every conditional treatment cell has probability at least \((1-\kappa_n)/2\ge7/16\).  The factorization caused by the common table therefore gives
\[
 p_{j,\ell}^{D,Y}(x,d,y)
 =p_{j,\ell}^{D}(x,d)m_{d,y}(x)
 \ge\frac7{16}\frac3{20}=\frac{21}{320}>\frac1{64}>v.
 \tag{21}
\]
Conditional variance and covariance decomposition applied to (20) give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(Y\mid X=x)
 =\frac{1-g_\star(x)^2}{4}
  +g_\star(x)^2\operatorname{Var}(D\mid X=x),
 \tag{22}
\]
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y,D\mid X=x)
 =g_\star(x)\operatorname{Var}(D\mid X=x).
 \tag{23}
\]
Since \(|g_\star|\le a\), (22) is at least
\[
 \frac{1-a^2}{4}=\frac{51}{400}>\frac1{64}>v.
 \tag{24}
\]
If \(V_D=\operatorname{Var}(D\mid X=x)>0\), then \(V_D\le1/4\), and (22)--(23) imply
\[
 |\operatorname{corr}(Y,D\mid X=x)|
 =\frac{|g_\star|\sqrt{V_D}}
        {\sqrt{(1-g_\star^2)/4+g_\star^2V_D}}
 \le\frac{a}{\sqrt{1-a^2}}
 =\frac7{\sqrt{51}}.
 \tag{25}
\]
Both sides are positive, and squaring shows
\[
 \frac{49}{51}<\frac{3969}{4096}
 \quad\text{because}\quad
 49\cdot4096=200704<202419=51\cdot3969.
\]
Hence \(7/\sqrt{51}<63/64<1-v\), where the last inequality uses \(v<1/64\).  If \(V_D=0\), (23) gives zero covariance, exactly as required by the convention in \(\mathrm{ass:observable\mbox{-}correlation\mbox{-}separation}\).  Equations (2)--(25) verify every member property in \(\mathrm{def:model\mbox{-}class}\), and therefore
\[
 \mathcal W_n\subset\mathcal P_n.
 \tag{26}
\]

Finally, under \(R_\star\), \(D\) is conditionally fair given \(X\), while the conditional outcome margin (20) is the same as under every \(P_{j,\ell}\).  Cancelling that strictly positive margin in the full observable density ratio gives, outside the null event \(X=c_{j,\ell}\),
\[
 L_{j,\ell}:=\frac{dP_{j,\ell}}{dR_\star}
 =1+(2D-1)\operatorname{sgn}(X-c_{j,\ell})w_{j,\ell}(X).
 \tag{27}
\]
This proves the asserted outcome invariance and \(\sigma(X,D)\)-measurability.  Direct integration gives
\[
 \int_{-1}^{1}\psi(u)^2\,du
 =2\left(1-\frac43+\frac65-\frac47+\frac19\right)
 =\frac{256}{315}.
 \tag{28}
\]
Conditioning on \(X\) under \(R_\star\) in (27) and using
\(E_{R_\star}[2D-1\mid X]=0\) shows
\[
 E_{R_\star}[L_{j,\ell}L_{k,r}]
 =1+\int_0^1
   \operatorname{sgn}(x-c_{j,\ell})
   \operatorname{sgn}(x-c_{k,r})
   w_{j,\ell}(x)w_{k,r}(x)\,dx.
 \tag{29}
\]
For distinct indices, (4) makes (29) equal to one.  For equal indices, the change of variables \(u=(x-c_{j,\ell})/h_n\) and (28) give
\[
 E_{R_\star}[L_{j,\ell}^2]
 =1+\frac{256}{315}\kappa_n^2h_n.
 \tag{30}
\]
Independence raises (29)--(30) to the \(n\)-th power.  Expanding the square of the equally weighted mixture likelihood ratio, with \(J_n\) diagonal and \(J_n(J_n-1)\) off-diagonal terms, yields
\[
 \chi^2(Q_{\ell,n},R_\star^{\otimes n})
 =\frac{\left(1+\frac{256}{315}\kappa_n^2h_n\right)^n-1}{J_n},
\]
as claimed.
body.justification: The explicit positivity, observable smoothness, variance, correlation, factorization, and second-moment calculations make outcome-assisted localization fail on a legal high-separation causal subexperiment.
body.gap: Aligned multivariate change-point analyses do not provide a monotone fuzzy-RD latent construction whose outcome margin cancels exactly while its two LATE labels are separated by \(7/5\).
body.consumer: The finite-sample lower theorem uses the family to transfer honesty between opposite effect labels without allowing the outcome channel to eliminate the location-entropy barrier.
